faq.html: Most of the questions below have no published answer from the FAA or ALPA. The National Academies asked for the underlying HIMS outcome data in 2023 and was told it would not be provided in full; what follows is assembled from program documents, court and arbitration records, and pilot accounts rather than from any dataset the program has released.
peth-false-positives.html: Phosphatidylethanol testing entered HIMS monitoring before the FAA formally advised examiners to use it in August 2020. Since then, false positives have been documented in a federal negligence suit that reached a jury verdict, in a Delta arbitration where the collection violated nearly every item on the laboratory's own protocol list, and in peer-reviewed work on vapour exposure and transfusion.
legal.html: The cases collected here were verified against primary records — dockets, opinions, and arbitration awards — rather than press summaries. Several are still moving: statuses that were accurate when first written have changed as motions were decided.
entering-hims.html: The decision points described below are the ones pilots report being least prepared for. Program documents describe the agreements as voluntary; the same documents describe the consequence of declining as loss of certification and employment.
hims-success-intro.html: The 85 percent figure traces to a 1993 study in Aviation, Space, and Environmental Medicine that measured how many pilots returned to flight duties after treatment, and reported a 13 percent relapse rate in the same paper. It has since been cited widely as a long-term abstinence rate, which is not what it measured.
dsm5-dependency-trap.html: The divergence is not theoretical. An NTSB administrative law judge set it out plainly in 2024: the DSM requires at least two criteria within the previous twelve months, while the federal aviation regulations require any one of four at any point in an airman's lifetime.
ntsb-cases.html: NTSB initial decisions are not published in the commercial legal databases, which is why this material is difficult to verify independently. Where possible the decisions themselves are cited by docket number rather than through secondary reporting.
writ-of-mandamus.html: Two mandamus and Freedom of Information Act actions concerning FAA aeromedical records, filed two years apart, were assigned to the same judge of the United States District Court for the District of Columbia.
